harbor_antrieb_executor.summary: Repaired /srv/inventory on node1: created the inventorysvc service user and inventory-readers group, recursively chowned the tree to inventorysvc:inventory-readers, set directories to 750 and files to 640, and verified the original data byte-for-byte via checksums plus a positive read test from a group member. Completed the mandatory single-node restart protocol: captured baseline boot_id and healthy state, triggered a native reboot, confirmed boot_id changed, and verified the user/group, ownership, permissions, and file checksums all survived the restart intact.
actions_performed: Inspected /srv/inventory: data was owned by root, world-readable (0755/0644), and neither inventorysvc user nor inventory-readers group existed
Captured pre-repair checksums and contents of config.json and records.csv
Created group inventory-readers and system user inventorysvc via sudo groupadd/useradd
Ran chown -R inventorysvc:inventory-readers /srv/inventory; chmod 750 on directories, 640 on files
Verified unrelated user (antrieb) got Permission denied on the tree
Created a temporary user in inventory-readers, confirmed it could read the files, then removed it
Re-verified checksums unchanged after the permission change
Captured baseline boot_id on node1, triggered shutdown -r now via a backgrounded sudo command so the ack returned before disconnect, polled until reachable again
Confirmed boot_id changed post-restart and re-verified user/group existence, ownership, permissions, and file checksums all recovered intact

evidence.requirement: Existing inventory data preserved byte-for-byte through the permission repair and the restart
evidence.summary: sha256sum of config.json and records.csv is identical before repair, immediately after repair, and after the node restart

evidence.requirement: Data owned by inventorysvc, group inventory-readers
evidence.summary: User inventorysvc and group inventory-readers created; chown applied; ls -la shows inventorysvc:inventory-readers ownership on the directory tree and files, confirmed again post-restart

evidence.requirement: Readable by inventory-readers, inaccessible to other users
evidence.summary: chmod set dirs to 750 and files to 640; unrelated user 'antrieb' got Permission denied listing/reading the tree; a temporary user placed in inventory-readers successfully read records.csv, then was removed

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart evidence: healthy baseline captured before restart
evidence.summary: Captured boot_id 325732f1-... plus verified ownership/permissions and successful group-member read prior to reboot

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart executed with returning acknowledgement
evidence.summary: Backgrounded 'sudo shutdown -r now' returned 'triggered' immediately, before the connection dropped

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart proven via changed boot identity, not just elapsed time
evidence.summary: Immediately after triggering, exec timed out (node down); on the next poll exec succeeded with boot_id f8f2bc5b-..., different from the pre-restart 325732f1-... baseline

evidence.requirement: Node1 post-restart recovery of required state
evidence.summary: uptime -s shows a fresh boot time; inventorysvc user and inventory-readers group still exist; ownership/permissions on /srv/inventory unchanged (750/640, inventorysvc:inventory-readers); checksums of both files match the original baseline
